pr.title: Fix tests for big-endian
pr.description:
The tests fail on s390x and presumably other big-endian systems, due to check of raw alloc values in the MIR output.

To fix the tests remove the raw bytes from the MIR output (via: compile-flags: -Zdump-mir-exclude-alloc-bytes) and update the matching diffs.

pr.author: fneddy

processing.reason: The PR makes no compiler optimization or program-semantics change. It only adds `-Zdump-mir-exclude-alloc-bytes` to three MIR-opt tests and rewrites their expected `ALLOCn` dumps from little-endian raw bytes to endian-independent `{ .. }` placeholders. The historically “incorrect” artifact is the golden test expectation’s endian dependence, not a transformation of Rust code. Any original/transformed function pair that differs numerically or behaviorally would therefore be an invented rewrite unsupported by the PR. Because the required pair must encode an actual historical wrong transformation with differing concrete results, no source-grounded pair can be validated here.

analysis.summary: MIR-opt GVN/RemoveZsts test expectations that embed raw ALLOC bytes are endian-dependent. This PR fixes those tests by adding `-Zdump-mir-exclude-alloc-bytes` and replacing byte dumps with size/align-only `{ .. }` placeholders. No compiler optimization transformation changed; the correction is to the test harness expectations.
analysis.trigger: Running MIR-opt GVN tests (including tests that also enable RemoveZsts or `-Zinline-mir`) on a big-endian target such as s390x when the expected `.diff` files contain raw allocation byte sequences.
preconditions: The test declares a MIR pass such as `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN`.
The expected MIR dump includes `ALLOCn (size: ..., align: ...) { ... }` blocks with explicit raw bytes.
The test is executed on a host/target whose endianness differs from the one used to generate the expectation.
analysis.originalLogic: The MIR test dumps included fixed raw allocation byte sequences in the expected output, for example `ALLOC0 (size: 4, align: 4)` followed by `01 00 00 00`, while the compile flags only enabled optimization passes such as `-Zmir-enable-passes=+RemoveZsts` or `-Zinline-mir`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: No optimization rewrite was historically incorrect. The incorrect transformation was in the test expectation layer: it treated the dumped raw allocation bytes as endian-independent, encoding little-endian bytes as expected output. On big-endian systems the same allocation dump differs, so the tests fail even though GVN/RemoveZsts behavior is unchanged. The fix removes those bytes from the dump rather than changing pass logic.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR-opt tests for GVN, including constant propagation, union-projection propagation, and loop-deref-mut cases; especially tests whose MIR output contains constant allocation blocks and which may also enable RemoveZsts or MIR inlining. The relevant input variation is host/target endianness, not the optimized program's semantics.
pitfalls: Raw ALLOC bytes in MIR dumps are endian-dependent and should not be used as portable golden output.
A passing little-endian expectation does not establish that the same `.diff` is valid on big-endian targets.
`-Zdump-mir-exclude-alloc-bytes` preserves allocation size and alignment but replaces the byte body with `..`; tests should still verify the relevant MIR statements and allocation shape.
Do not infer an optimization correctness bug from a big-endian diff failure when only byte order/raw allocation rendering differs.
analysis.testStrategy: Add `-Zdump-mir-exclude-alloc-bytes` to the affected tests' `//@ compile-flags`, then update expected `ALLOCn` sections from explicit byte dumps to forms like `ALLOC0 (size: 4, align: 4) { .. }` and `ALLOC0 (size: 8, align: 4) { .. }`. Keep the pass/behavior assertions intact so GVN/RemoveZsts coverage is unchanged while the golden output becomes endian-independent. Exercise the test suite on a big-endian target such as s390x and compare against the same pass output with allocation bytes excluded.
evidence: The tests fail on s390x and presumably other big-endian systems, due to check of raw alloc values in the MIR output.
To fix the tests remove the raw bytes from the MIR output (via: compile-flags: -Zdump-mir-exclude-alloc-bytes) and update the matching diffs.
